facts.text: The first rendezvous of white traders and trappers in the Rocky Mountains took place in July 1825 just north of McKinnon.
McKinnon emerged as a named community in 1922, evolving from earlier informal settlements known as Coon Hollow and Mountain Home.
Located at an elevation of about 7,000 feet, McKinnon is known for its ranching economy and agricultural roots.
The completion of the Union Pacific Railroad in 1869 improved market access and profoundly influenced the development of the McKinnon area.
Mormon pioneers from Utah helped grow the community starting around 1915, establishing claims and building irrigation canals in the valley.
Early settlers in McKinnon built a cooperative community initially known as Terry Town, focusing on cattle, sheep, and hay production.
